content.one_sentence_role: Separates radial variation from the change of unit direction to obtain the global bound with coefficient 1 + 2.
content.natural_language_statement:
For real normed spaces $X,Y$ and a bijective chord-metric isometry $\Delta:S_X\to S_Y$, define $R_\Delta(0)=0$ and $R_\Delta(x)=\|x\|\Delta(x/\|x\|)$ for $x\ne0$. Here $S_X=\{u\in X:\|u\|=1\}$ and $S_Y=\{v\in Y:\|v\|=1\}$ are the unit spheres. Then for every $x,y\in X$,

$$\|R_\Delta(x)-R_\Delta(y)\|\le3\|x-y\|.$$
content.assumptions: The sphere distances are inherited from the ambient norms. The map $\Delta$ is a bijective isometry, so it preserves these chord distances and sends unit vectors to unit vectors. No completeness, finite-dimensionality or nontriviality assumption is made.
content.conclusion: The forward radial map is globally $3$-Lipschitz. Applying the same theorem to $\Delta^{-1}$ gives the separately stated $3$-Lipschitz bound for $R_{\Delta^{-1}}$. Together with the inverse identities, this makes the radial bijection a homeomorphism with Lipschitz inverse.
content.proof_summary:
First assume $0<\|y\|\le\|x\|$, and put $\widehat x=x/\|x\|$, $\widehat y=y/\|y\|$. Split the difference at the smaller radius:

$$\begin{aligned}
R_\Delta(x)-R_\Delta(y)
&=(\|x\|-\|y\|)\Delta(\widehat x)\\
&\quad+\|y\|\bigl(\Delta(\widehat x)-\Delta(\widehat y)\bigr).
\end{aligned}$$

The first direction has norm one and $\Delta$ preserves chord distances. Hence

$$\begin{aligned}
\|R_\Delta(x)-R_\Delta(y)\|
&\le |\|x\|-\|y\||+\|y\|\|\widehat x-\widehat y\|\\
&\le\|x-y\|+2\|x-y\|=3\|x-y\|.
\end{aligned}$$

The first bound is the reverse triangle inequality. The second uses the angular lemma with its three hypotheses $x\ne0$, $y\ne0$ and $\|y\|\le\|x\|$. The following calculation gives its coefficient $2$.

proof_steps.text:
Set $r=\|y\|/\|x\|$. The assumed order and positivity imply $0\le r\le1$ and $r\|x\|=\|y\|$. Scaling the normalized difference gives

$$\|y\|(\widehat x-\widehat y)=rx-y=r(x-y)+(r-1)y.$$

Consequently $\|y\|\|\widehat x-\widehat y\|=\|rx-y\|$.

The first summand satisfies $\|r(x-y)\|=r\|x-y\|\le\|x-y\|$. For the second,

$$\begin{aligned}
\|(r-1)y\|&=(1-r)\|y\|\\
&\le(1-r)\|x\|=\|x\|-\|y\|\\
&\le\|x-y\|.
\end{aligned}$$

The triangle inequality now yields $\|rx-y\|\le2\|x-y\|$, which is the required angular bound.

Insert this angular bound into the displayed radial decomposition. If the norm order is reversed, interchange $x,y$ and use the symmetry of $\|x-y\|$ and of the image distance. If one vector is zero, norm preservation gives the sharper equality $\|R_\Delta(x)-R_\Delta(0)\|=\|x\|$, so the bound by $3\|x\|$ follows; the two-zero case is immediate.

content.lean_realization_notes: The constant $3$ is a proved upper bound. This statement makes no optimality assertion and supplies no ambient distance-preserving or linear-extension conclusion. Both directions of the homeomorphism use the same radial maps as in the definitions.
